member.name: T:TingenWebService.Core.Trove.BluePrint
member.summary: User-modifiable templates.

remarks.note:
Blueprints are essentially templates for output generated by the Tingen Web Service. They are used to format logs,error messages, and other data in a consistent manner.
When the Tingen Web Service is initialized, these templates are exported to the blueprints\ folder. The external templates can then be modified by the user to customize the log output.

To restore a template to its original state:
Delete the template file from the blueprints folder
Restart the Tingen Web Service.
The original template will be copied back to the blueprints folder.

member.name: M:TingenWebService.Core.Trove.BluePrint.ErrorLogTxtBP
member.summary: Build the blueprint for text error logs.

remarks.note:
Logs can be exported using any of the following formats:
Plain text
+ Smallest file size (good for raw speed)
+ Can be opened in any text editor
+ Easy to customize
- Does not support any formatting/styling (totally boring!)
- Super compact, not the easiest to read
Markdown
+ Allows for formatting, so logs look nice and are easy to read
+ Super easy to customize
+ The coolest format!
- Not as widely supported as plain text (some text editors may not support it)
- Probably not the best choice for emailing logs
HTML
+ Allows for complex formatting
+ Can be opened in any web browser (and most email clients)
- Largest file size
- More difficult to customize than plain text or markdown
In general:
Use plain text it you aren't constantly looking at logs.
Use Markdown if you are constantly looking at logs.
Use HTML if you are emailing logs.

member.returns: The text error log template string.

member.summary: The main entry method for the Tingen Web Service.
member.param: The OptionObject sent from Avatar.
The Script Parameter sent from Avatar.
member.remarks:
This is where the following magic happens:
Verify that Avatar actually sent data (and return the unmodified OptionObject if not)
StartApp() sets up the Tingen Web Service session
The request is processed
The session is logged
The (potentially) modified OptionObject is returned to Avatar
The reason that all of this logic is here is because this way the CompletedOptionObject is returned to Avatar from a single location, regardless of whether the request was successful or not.
This method is required by Avatar.
member.returns: A (potentially modified) completed OptionObject.

The Script Parameter sent from Avatar.

remarks.note:
Avatar sends two pieces of data to the Tingen Web Service:
The SentOptionObject
The SentScriptParameter
If either of these components are missing, the Tingen Web Service cannot function properly. This method checks for the presence of both components and logs an error if either is missing.
